intentional_differences.subject: retired atoms
intentional_differences.description: Ten legacy atoms have no enforcement point (no route, task or screen requires them). They are preserved in rbac_legacy_map as retired; the roles that hold them lose nothing that any code checks.

intentional_differences.subject: superadmin
intentional_differences.description: Legacy superadmin passes by role name (and holds a row per atom on the live database). The new role holds every active permission as materialised grants; there is no wildcard and no bypass.

intentional_differences.subject: name checks become permissions
intentional_differences.description: 7 role-name checks become platform- or organisation-scope permissions held only by the superadmin role, so their holders are unchanged.

intentional_differences.subject: new governance permissions
intentional_differences.description: Permissions with no legacy counterpart (RBAC governance). Only the superadmin role holds them, so no live user gains a capability.

intentional_differences.subject: cross-organisation visibility
intentional_differences.description: Legacy superadmin sees every organisation's data on list endpoints through per-router role-name helpers. That is scope, not a permission, and the RBAC-2 catalogue does not model it; RBAC-5 decides how platform-scope assignments reach other organisations.

intentional_differences.subject: live-only atom
intentional_differences.description: audit_logs:read exists on the live database (held by superadmin and org_admin) but not in the seed. It is retired with the rest; no code reads it.

intentional_differences.subject: assignment hierarchy
intentional_differences.description: Legacy: an org_admin cannot assign the superadmin role (a role-name check). New: the escalation ceiling and platform.role.assign_platform express the same rule.
